questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of 'elements - valency' is correct?

I. Boron - 2

II. Fluorine -3
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fluorine** has a **valency of 1 **because it needs to gain only **one electron** to achieve a** stable electron configuration of 8 valence electrons.**
 
• **Boron** has a** valency of 3** because it tends to lose its** three valence electrons **to achieve a stable electron configuration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Valency,** also known as** oxidation number,** is a **measure of an element's combining capacity** or the** number of electrons it can gain, lose, or share when forming chemical compounds.**
 
• It determines** how an element will bond with other elements to form compounds.**
 
• The valency of an element is determined by the** number of valence electrons it possesses.**
 
• **Valence** electrons are the electrons present in the outermost energy level or shell of an atom.
 
• These electrons are involved in **chemical reactions** and have the potential to participate in** bonding**.

questions.question: Which of the following has the highest boiling point?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alkynes.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alkynes:-**

 
 
• **​**These have the **highest boiling point **among the given options due to their** strong intermolecular forces of attraction.**
 
• Alkynes have **triple bonds** between carbon atoms, which results in a **linear shape **and** close packing of molecules**, leading to** strong van der Waals forces.**
 
• **Alkanes** have **weaker intermolecular forces **due to their **single bonds** and** branched structures**, resulting in **lower boiling points.**
 
• **Alkenes **have** double bonds**, which create a kink in the molecule and reduce the surface area available for intermolecular interactions, leading to **lower boiling points.**
 
• **Free carbon dioxide** is a gas at room temperature and pressure, and hence, it has the** lowest boiling point** among the given options.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkanes**: 

 
 
• These are hydrocarbons with **single bonds** between carbon atoms, and their **boiling points increase** with** increasing chain length **and **molecular weight.**
 
 
 
• **Alkenes: **
 
 
• **​**These are hydrocarbons with **double bonds** between carbon atoms, and their** boiling points are lower** than those of corresponding alkanes due to their lower intermolecular forces.
 
 
 
• **Free carbon dioxide:** 
 
 
• It is a **gas at room temperature **and pressure and is formed during **respiration, combustion,** and other processes. 
 
 
• It has a boiling point of **-78.5oC** at standard temperature and pressure.

questions.question: In the year 1817 ______ tried to arrange elements with similar properties into groups.
questions.solution:

• Dobereiner Triad is based on three elements group. He was the first person who started grouping of elements on the basis of atomic weight.
 
• The three elements of the triad were arranged in such a manner that the atomic mass of the middle element was approximately the average of the atomic masses of the other two elements.

questions.question: _________ is associated with spoilage, development of off-flavors, deterioration of textures, discoloration and loss of nutritional value.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**food deterioration**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Food deterioration:-**

__
 
• **It is a natural process that occurs over time in all foods. **
 
• **It is caused by a variety of factors, including:**
 
 
• **Microorganisms**: Bacteria, yeasts, and molds can grow on food and cause it to spoil.
 
• **Enzymes**: Enzymes are naturally occurring proteins that speed up chemical reactions. In food, enzymes can cause food to break down and spoil.
 
• **Oxygen**: Oxygen can cause food to oxidize and become rancid.
 
• **Light**: Light can cause food to discolor and lose nutrients.
 
• **Temperature**: Temperature can affect the rate of food deterioration. Food spoils more quickly at warm temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Food deterioration can cause a variety of problems, including:**
 
 
• **Spoilage**: Spoiled food is unsafe to eat and can cause food poisoning.
 
• **Off-flavors**: Food that is starting to deteriorate may develop off-flavors, such as sourness, bitterness, or staleness.
 
• **Deterioration of textures**: Food that is deteriorating may become slimy, mushy, or tough.
 
• **Discoloration**: Food that is deteriorating may change color, such as browning or fading.
 
• **Loss of nutritional value: **Food that is deteriorating may lose some of its nutrients.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Food processing:-**

 
 
• It can be any method used to turn raw food into food products.
 
• It can involve one or a combination of the following: washing, chopping, pasteurizing, freezing, fermenting, packaging, and more.
 
 
 
• **Food preservation:-**
 
 
• It is the process of treating and handling food to prevent or slow down its spoilage. 
 
 
 
• **Food conservation:-**
 
 
• It is the practice of keeping food fresh and edible for as long as possible.

questions.question: According to Newland's Law of Octaves, every eighth element has properties similar to those of the first element. Which of the following elements has properties similar to those of N?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newlands' Law of Octaves:**

 
 
• John Newlands, an English chemist, proposed the Law of Octaves in 1865.
 
• He arranged the known elements in order of increasing atomic mass.
 
• He observed that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, much like the octaves in music.
 
• This law was an early attempt to find patterns in the properties of elements.
 
• The law was based on the atomic weights of the elements known at that time.
 
• The law was only applicable to elements up to calcium.
 
• Beyond calcium, the law failed because heavier elements did not follow the pattern.
 
• The periodic table was not fully developed at the time of Newlands.
 
• The later discovery of noble gases, also disrupted the octaves.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nitrogen (N) and Phosphorus (P):**

 
 
• Nitrogen and Phosphorus belong to Group 15 (also known as the Nitrogen group or pnictogens) of the periodic table.
 
• They have similar chemical properties due to their similar electron configurations.
 
• Both have five valence electrons, which are the electrons in the outermost shell.
 
• This similarity in valence electrons leads to similar bonding behavior.
 
• Both can form covalent bonds.
 
• Both can form compounds with similar formulas.
 
• Both can have multiple oxidation states.
 
• Both are non-metals.
 
• Nitrogen and phosphorus are essential elements for life.
 
• They both can form acids.
 
• They both can form oxides.

questions.question: How many elements are there in the periodic table such that for every element name there is a single alphabet that symbolically represents it (for example, B-Boron, C-Carbon, etc)?
questions.solution:
**The Correct Answer is __Option 3__ i.e 14.**

 
• The periodic table is a tabular display of the chemical elements, which are arranged by atomic number, electron configuration, and recurring chemical properties.
 
• **Elements are arranged from left to right** and **top to bottom** in order of **increasing atomic number**. The order generally coincides with increasing atomic mass.
 
• The rows are called **periods**. The number of electrons in a period increases as one moves down the periodic table; therefore, as the energy level of the atom increases, the number of energy sub-levels per energy level increases.

 Elements that occupy the same column on the periodic table (called a "group") have identical valance electron configurations and consequently behave in a similar fashion chemically. For instance, all the group 18 elements are inert gases.
 
• There are **14 elements in the periodic table**, represented by a single letter. They are

questions.question: Hydrogen ions cannot exist alone, but they exist after combining with water molecules. Which of the following is the correct way to show hydrogen ions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** H3O+**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **hydrogen ions (H⁺) combine with water molecules**, they form a hydronium ion (H₃O⁺).
 
• This is **because H⁺ ions are essentially protons **(which are just hydrogen nuclei) and cannot exist freely in aqueous solutions.
 
• They interact with **water molecules to form hydronium ions.**
 
• The hydronium ion **represents the protonated form of water and is the actual species responsible for the acidic properties in aqueous solution**s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **HO⁻ (Hydroxide Ion)**

 
 
• **​**The hydroxide ion (OH⁻) is formed when a **water molecule (H₂O)** loses a proton (H⁺).
 
• The hydroxide ion is characteristic of **basic (alkaline)** solutions.
 
• It acts as a **base** because it can accept a proton (H⁺).
 
• Therefore, HO⁻ is associated with **basicity** or **alkalinity** rather than acidity.
 
• For example, in a strong base like sodium hydroxide (NaOH), the OH⁻ ions are responsible for the basicity.
 
 
 
• **H₂ (Hydrogen Gas)** 
 
 
• H₂ is a **molecule of hydrogen gas**, which consists of two hydrogen atoms (H) bonded together by a covalent bond
 
• Hydrogen gas (H₂) is **neutral** in nature and is not related to the concept of **acidity** or **alkalinity**.
 
• It is a **molecular species**
 
 
 
• **H₂SO₄ (Sulfuric Acid)**
 
 
• **​**H₂SO₄ is** sulfuric acid, a strong acid that dissociates in water to release hydrogen ions (H⁺).**
 
• Sulfuric acid is one of the **strongest acids**.
 
• When it dissolves in water, it releases a significant amount of **hydrogen ions (H⁺)**, which lowers the pH and makes the solution **acidic**.
 
• However, sulfuric acid itself is not a direct representation of hydrogen ions in their purest form; it is a compound that produces H⁺ ions in solution.

questions.question: 'At constant temperature, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is proportional to the partial pressure of the gas collected above the surface of the liquid or solution'. What is this rule?
questions.solution:
Option** 1 **is correct, i.e. __**Henry's law**__.

__
 
• **Henry’s law**__, states that the weight of a gas dissolved by a liquid is proportional to the pressure of the gas upon the liquid.
 
• The law, which was first formulated in **1803** by the English physician and chemist **William Henry**, holds only for dilute solutions and low gas pressures.

**Extra facts:**

 
• **Charles' law:** A law stating that the volume of an ideal gas at constant pressure is directly proportional to the absolute temperature.
 
• **Boyle's law:** A law stating that the pressure of a given mass of an ideal gas is inversely proportional to its volume at a constant temperature.
 
• Newton's law:
 
 
• **Newton’s first law:** states that, if a body is at rest or moving at a constant speed in a straight line, it will remain at rest or keep moving in a straight line at constant speed unless it is acted upon by a force.
 
• **Newton’s second law**: States that the time rate of change of the momentum of a body is equal in both magnitude and direction to the force imposed on it.
 
• **Newton’s third law:** states that when two bodies interact, they apply forces to one another that are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

questions.question:
Select the correct order of processes used for water purification in waterworks.

1. Filtration

2. Chlorination

3. Suspended impurity sedimentation

4. Solid impurity sedimentation
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4-3-1-2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The correct sequence for water purification in waterworks is: **solid impurity sedimentation → suspended impurity sedimentation → filtration → chlorination**.
 
• **Solid impurity sedimentation**: Involves allowing larger particles and debris to settle at the bottom of the tank.
 
• **Suspended impurity sedimentation**: Addition of coagulants like alum helps smaller particles clump together and settle.
 
• **Filtration**: Water passes through sand, gravel, and other filter media to remove fine particles and impurities.
 
• **Chlorination**: Disinfection by adding chlorine to eliminate harmful microorganisms and pathogens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coagulation and Flocculation**:

 
 
• These are essential processes where chemicals like alum are added to water to aggregate suspended particles into larger flocs.
 
• Flocs settle faster during sedimentation, improving water clarity.
 
 
 
• **Chlorination**:
 
 
• A widely used disinfection technique in water treatment plants.
 
• It effectively kills bacteria, viruses, and other microbes, ensuring safe drinking water.
 
 
 
• **Filtration Media**:
 
 
• Common filtration materials include sand, gravel, and activated carbon.
 
• These materials help in trapping fine particles and adsorbing organic impurities.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Sedimentation**:
 
 
• Reduces the load on downstream filtration systems by removing large and suspended impurities early in the process.
 
• Enhances the efficiency of the entire water purification process.
